title: Migrating Plugins and Custom Utilities
subtopics: Replacing suitable extensions with CSS-first utilities
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of migrating plugins and custom utilities.
Apply one appropriate technique to a small Tailwind CSS example.
Verify the expected result and identify a common failure mode.

content.intro: In this lesson, focus on migrating plugins and custom utilities and connect it to the way Tailwind CSS generates and applies utility styles.
content.why_it_matters: Migrating Plugins and Custom Utilities protects existing projects from accidental regressions when framework versions and build workflows differ.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: The source curriculum highlights: Reviewing custom plugin APIs; Identifying supported legacy plugins; Replacing suitable extensions with CSS-first utilities; Testing variant compatibility; Avoiding unsupported configuration assumptions. Treat these as practical decisions rather than a list to memorize: identify the intended behavior, choose the smallest suitable utility or directive, and inspect what the browser receives.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with the example, change one decision related to migrating plugins and custom utilities, then compare the outcome. In a Tailwind-enabled project, confirm the generated CSS exists; class strings alone do not make styles available without a configured build.

content_blocks.title: Version and compatibility note
content_blocks.text: This course prioritizes Tailwind CSS v4. Confirm your installed version and use its matching official guide. Snippets using v3 directives or configuration are labelled as legacy and should not be mixed blindly with v4 syntax.

content.task: Create a minimal example demonstrating migrating plugins and custom utilities. Include a before/after comparison and explain why the chosen utility, variant or directive is appropriate.
task_acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate at least one decision tied to migrating plugins and custom utilities.
Keep the example easy to inspect, with complete utility names.
Test the outcome and document one limitation or environment assumption.
hints: Identify which listed syllabus topic is most important to migrating plugins and custom utilities.
Change one utility, token, variant or configuration setting at a time.
Inspect generated CSS and computed styles before changing unrelated code.
content.expected_output: A migration is reviewed through a successful build, visual regression checks and documented manual changes.
troubleshooting: If no style appears, verify the package, CSS import and build-tool integration before changing the HTML.
If only a state or breakpoint style fails, check the full class token, source detection, condition and computed CSS.
For a framework snippet, import the stylesheet through its supported entry point and consult the current official guide.
common_mistakes: Applying migrating plugins and custom utilities without checking generated styles or browser behavior.
Mixing Tailwind v3 and v4 setup examples without a migration plan.
Treating visual appearance as a substitute for semantic markup, keyboard usability or actual component behavior.
summary: Migrating Plugins and Custom Utilities is one part of a predictable utility-first styling workflow.
Keep examples small, test the built interface and use version-matched documentation.
